where_the_thread_broke: THREE independent breaks, all upstream of the ActorChip render: (1) src/db/org.ts::listOrgTree's empRows SQL never selected e.deactivated_at and the OrgPerson type carried no such field, so GET /api/org's people[] physically could not carry the signal; (2) web/src/forms/field-renderer.jsx::fetchEmployees()'s flatten step (`employees.push({id, name, position})`) explicitly listed only 3 fields, so even had the API started sending `deactivated` it would have been silently dropped a second time before reaching screen-app-records.jsx's employeesById Map; (3) [B1, judge round 2] web/src/screens/screen-record-detail.jsx built its authorNames map as id → name STRING (narrowing each entry to just e.name) and PersonFieldValue passed no deactivated prop to ActorChip at all — so after fixing (1)+(2) alone, a deactivated executor was correctly muted in the record LIST (PersonCell) but rendered as active in the DETAIL view of the same record, one click apart. Fixing any subset would not have worked — verified by mutation-proof for (1) (git stash of src/db/org.ts alone made the new DB test fail red) and by the judge's B1 finding for (3).

b1_round.finding: Judge changes_requested B1: screen-record-detail.jsx:772 built authorNames = new Map(list.map((e) => [e.id, e.name])) — names only; PersonFieldValue (:629-632) rendered person fields through the same ActorChip but WITHOUT a deactivated prop. Round 1 therefore introduced a visible inconsistency: deactivated executor muted in the record list, active-looking in the detail of the same record.
b1_round.fix: authorNames now holds WHOLE employee entries ({id, name, position, deactivated}) built via buildEmployeesById — a new shared helper exported from web/src/forms/field-renderer.jsx (the ONE canonical fetchEmployees-list → Map step, tolerant of non-array input). PersonFieldValue reads hit.name / hit.deactivated and threads deactivated into ActorChip with the identical boolean semantics PersonCell uses. screen-app-records.jsx switched from its inline Map literal to the same helper.
b1_round.authorNames_readers_audit: Exactly two readers existed in screen-record-detail.jsx (verified by grep over every authorNames occurrence in the file): (1) PersonFieldValue — updated to the entry shape + deactivated threading; (2) the created_by sidebar line `formatPersonName(authorNames.get(record.created_by))` — updated to `.get(...)?.name` (without this it would have silently regressed the author display to the raw slug: formatPersonName of a non-string returns null). ?.name preserves the missing-entry degrade byte-for-byte (undefined → formatPersonName null → `|| record.created_by` raw-slug fallback). No other file imports PersonFieldValue (grep: only its own test file). No other consumer of fetchEmployees narrows the list (PersonPicker reads .id/.name/.position off the list directly; screen-rights.jsx has its own unrelated local fetchEmployees).
b1_round.n1_nit: RESOLVED (not deferred): the e2e tests no longer copy the Map-construction expression as a literal — both screens' useEffects AND all three e2e tests (field-renderer-t0649, screen-app-records, screen-record-detail) call the SAME exported buildEmployeesById, so a screen can no longer drift to a narrower value shape without its test exercising that exact drift. Wiring source-text tests pin `setEmployeesById(buildEmployeesById(list))` / `setAuthorNames(buildEmployeesById(list))`, and the detail wiring test asserts the old `[e.id, e.name]` narrowing stays gone from the screen source.

decision_boolean_vs_date: Boolean `deactivated`, never the raw `deactivated_at` epoch-ms timestamp. Two reasons: (a) privacy/minimization — GET /api/org is broadly readable by ANY authenticated tenant member (plain withAuth, no mgmt_object:* gate; it powers PersonPicker for every record form), so exposing the EXACT deactivation timestamp to every coworker is more than the product case ("see that the executor left") needs; (b) consistency with the one existing precedent — src/db/actor-resolver.ts::batchResolveActors (T-0648), which already surfaces this exact signal to ActorChip on audit/inbox/grant-trail as `ResolvedActor.deactivated: row.deactivated_at != null`, a boolean. ActorChip's own prop contract is `deactivated: boolean`. Emitting a raw date here would have created a second, inconsistent contract for the same visual signal — the kind of parallel-resolver drift D-064/T-0658 already warn against.
why_old_test_was_false: web/src/screens/screen-app-records.test.jsx's 'threads deactivated through when the batch entry carries it' (T-0673) built its `employees` Map BY HAND: `new Map([['emp-slug-1', {id, name, deactivated: true}]])`. That fixture is never produced by any real code path — it proves only that PersonCell forwards a `deactivated` key IF one is already on its map entry, never that the REAL map (built by screen-app-records.jsx from fetchEmployees()'s real /api/org response) ever HAS that key. Before this fix it never did, so the feature was fully inert in production behind an all-green test suite. Fix: kept the old test (a legitimate, narrow unit test of PersonCell's own prop-threading contract — deleting it loses real regression coverage on PersonCell itself), added a comment above it naming the limitation, and added honest e2e tests that mock globalThis.fetch with a realistic /api/org payload, call the REAL fetchEmployees(), build the Map via the SAME shared buildEmployeesById the screens call, and only then exercise PersonCell/PersonFieldValue — these fail on pre-fix code. Also extended field-renderer-t0649.test.jsx's exact-shape `toEqual` test (which pins the literal output object of fetchEmployees()) to include `deactivated: false` so any future re-narrowing of the flatten step fails mutationally.
